summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old female with a history of type I diabetes, end-stage renal disease with prior kidney and pancreas transplants, and severe mitral regurgitation was admitted for worsening heart failure symptoms. She underwent elective coronary artery bypass grafting x3 and mechanical mitral valve replacement. The surgery was performed due to severe three-vessel coronary disease and ischemic mitral regurgitation. She tolerated the procedure well, was extubated on postoperative day one, and transitioned to the telemetry floor. Her renal function remained stable throughout admission, and she was managed on warfarin for mechanical valve anticoagulation. By discharge on postoperative day six, she was ambulating with assistance, pain was controlled with oral medications, and incisions were healing. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with detailed instructions on wound care, activity restrictions, and medication management.
